overview: Stockland is one of Australia's largest diversified property groups, structured as a stapled security (one Stockland Corporation share plus one Stockland Trust unit) that has provided end-to-end exposure to the property lifecycle for over 40 years. The Group operates two complementary segments -- Investment Management (recurring rental and fee income from Logistics, Workplace and Town Centre/Retail assets) and Development (residential Masterplanned Communities, Land Lease Communities, and Commercial Development including logistics and an emerging Data Centres platform). Stockland fully exited Retirement Living via the ~$987m EQT Infrastructure sale (announced Feb 2022, plus smaller divestments to Prime Value and Qualitas), reshaping the portfolio around residential-for-sale, land lease, logistics/workplace and essentials-based retail.

business_model.summary: Stockland earns high-quality recurring income from its investment property portfolio (Logistics, Workplace, Retail Town Centres) plus development profit and fee income from selling residential lots (Masterplanned Communities), land lease home sites, and commercial/logistics assets, increasingly via capital-partnering structures where third-party institutional capital co-invests and Stockland earns development and funds/property management fees. Target capital allocation is 70-80% recurring / 20-30% development, with an income mix target of 60% recurring / 40% development (FY26 actual: 73%/27% capital allocation, 61%/39% income mix).

revenue_streams.name: Investment Management - Retail (Town Centres)
revenue_streams.notes: FFO $334m in FY26, up 4.5% YoY; ~$5.0bn portfolio, 34% of portfolio weighting

revenue_streams.name: Investment Management - Logistics
revenue_streams.notes: FFO $179m in FY26, up 3.8%; comparable growth 8.1%; ~$3.4bn portfolio, 27% weighting

revenue_streams.name: Investment Management - Workplace
revenue_streams.notes: FFO $114m in FY26, up 2.7%; occupancy down to 86.6% from 91.1%; being recycled toward change-of-use/apartments

revenue_streams.name: Development - Masterplanned Communities (MPC)
revenue_streams.notes: Development FFO $535m in FY26 (+2.4%); 8,902 lot settlements (+30%); largest single earnings driver

revenue_streams.name: Development - Land Lease Communities (LLC)
revenue_streams.notes: Development FFO $100m (+67%); 777 settlements (+48%); FY27 guidance 850-950 settlements

revenue_streams.name: Commercial Development (incl. Data Centres)
revenue_streams.notes: FFO $35m in FY26 vs $6m FY25; Data Centres platform (EdgeConneX JV) expected to contribute FFO from FY27

revenue_streams.name: Fee income (funds/development/property management)
revenue_streams.notes: $119m in FY26, up 20%, reflecting scaling of capital-partnering platform

business_model.customer_type: B2C (home buyers, retail shoppers, land lease residents) and B2B (retail/logistics/workplace tenants, institutional capital partners such as M&G, Invesco, Mercer, Morgan Stanley Real Estate Investing, EdgeConneX)
business_model.geographic_mix: Entirely Australia-domestic; diversified across NSW, Qld, Vic and WA, with growth skew toward Qld/WA residential markets in FY26

competitive_position.market_position: One of Australia's largest diversified real estate groups and the ASX-listed developer with the greatest exposure to the masterplanned community model; a leading residential land developer (record settlement year in FY26) with a smaller but growing logistics, workplace, retail and land-lease investment portfolio

moat_factors.description: 51 masterplanned communities and 37 land lease communities across four states give multi-year visibility (3,824+ MPC contracts on hand at average price above FY26 settlements) and negotiating power with governments and trade contractors

moat_factors.factor: Capital partnering platform / brand with institutional capital
moat_factors.description: Deep relationships with M&G, Invesco, Mercer, Morgan Stanley Real Estate Investing and EdgeConneX allow Stockland to recycle capital, earn high-margin recurring fee income (fee income +20% in FY26) and scale development beyond its own balance sheet
A3/stable Moody's rating, gearing of 22.7% (within 20-30% target) and $3.2bn liquidity support countercyclical land acquisition and development funding through housing downturns
End-to-end capability spanning origination, development, leasing and asset/funds management differentiates from pure-play residential developers or pure-play REITs
>70% of retail portfolio income from essentials-based categories provides resilience against discretionary spending swings

weaknesses: Greater exposure to the Australian residential land/housing cycle than most listed landlord peers (Mirvac, GPT, Dexus are more investment-portfolio weighted)
Workplace/office portfolio in structural decline (occupancy fell to 86.6% in FY26) and is being run down/repositioned rather than grown
Data Centres and Commercial Development are nascent and unproven at scale relative to specialist players like Goodman/NEXTDC
Development earnings (~60%+ of FFO) are inherently lower-quality/non-recurring versus pure rental income peers, creating earnings volatility tied to settlement timing

growth_drivers: Step-change in Masterplanned Communities and Land Lease Communities settlement volumes, with FY27 guidance of 7,300-8,300 MPC lots and 850-950 LLC home sites and substantial contracts on hand providing revenue visibility

Data Centres platform (Stockland EdgeConneX 50/50 partnership) with ~450MW of power secured across three sites and further pipeline in NSW/Victoria, expected to start contributing FFO in FY27 and monetize via revaluation over time
Expanding capital-partnering platform (M&G, Invesco, Mercer, Morgan Stanley Real Estate Investing) driving ~20% growth in fee income and enabling higher-return, lower-capital-intensity growth
Logistics portfolio releasing spreads of 33.8% and continued east-coast industrial demand supporting comparable FFO growth of 8.1%
Structural housing undersupply and population growth in Australia supporting medium-term normalisation of residential demand
New-build exemption from the incoming (July 2027) negative gearing changes is a relative tailwind for greenfield MPC/LLC lot sales versus established dwellings
Commercial Development pipeline of ~$16bn end value (logistics, mixed-use/workplace, retail, community real estate) provides a long runway for future earnings and fee income

business.description: MPC and LLC settlements are the largest FFO contributor; buyer sentiment has already moderated in 2H FY26 amid cumulative rate rises and tax-change uncertainty, and FY27 guidance embeds a lower MPC FFO contribution than FY26
Occupancy fell from 91.1% to 86.6% in FY26; portfolio is being progressively repositioned/divested (e.g., 601 Pacific Highway conversion to apartments) rather than grown

business.risk: Execution risk on new growth platforms
business.description: Data Centres, Commercial Development and expanded capital partnerships are relatively new/unproven at scale and depend on continued institutional capital appetite and successful site conversion (power, planning approvals)
MPC development operating margin fell from 22.9% to 21.2% in FY26 due to mix shift to lower-margin projects and rising marketing costs

financial.description: Weighted average cost of debt expected to rise from 5.3% in FY26 to ~5.9% in FY27 (assuming ~4.6% average BBSW); fixed hedge ratio fell from 76% to 65% in FY26, increasing floating-rate exposure

Gearing of 22.7% (look-through 24.4%) is comfortably within the 20-30%/<35% targets, but statutory profit is significantly influenced by investment property revaluations (+$202m in FY26), which can reverse in a downturn

Distribution Reinvestment Plan was suspended for 2H26 and the payout ratio range was recalibrated to 60-80% of FFO (from a tighter historical band) to fund growth, which could pressure the dividend/distribution narrative if FFO growth disappoints

regulatory.description: MPC, LLC and Data Centre pipeline conversion depend on state/local planning approvals; NSW Investment Delivery Authority fast-track process mitigates but does not eliminate this risk

The 2024 ACCC review of the Stockland/Supalai acquisition of Lendlease's masterplanned communities portfolio (cleared subject to divestiture of the Forest Reach project) illustrates regulatory sensitivity to further residential-sector consolidation

regulatory.risk: Tax policy changes affecting residential investment demand
regulatory.description: Australian Federal Budget (May 2026) abolishes negative gearing for established dwellings purchased after 12 May 2026 from 1 July 2027, alongside CGT discount reform; new-build exemptions are a relative positive for Stockland's MPC/LLC product but the broader policy shift adds uncertainty to established-market pricing and investor demand dynamics

regulatory.risk: Climate disclosure and decarbonisation compliance costs
regulatory.description: New mandatory AASB S2 climate reporting requirements add compliance cost, though Stockland already achieved net zero Scope 1 & 2 in FY26

macro.description: RBA resumed a tightening cycle in February 2026; higher mortgage rates (~6.25-6.4% by mid-2026) directly affect affordability and settlement timing for MPC/LLC buyers and raise Stockland's own funding costs

macro.risk: Consumer sentiment and discretionary retail spending
macro.description: Discretionary retail category sales have become more volatile reflecting weaker consumer sentiment, though >70% essentials-based weighting cushions the Retail portfolio
KPMG forecasts a modest (~1.1%) national house price decline in 2026 before recovery in 2027; a sharper downturn would compress MPC margins and delay settlements
Elevated build costs affect development margins and the economics of new logistics/data centre/residential product

macro_factors.industry_outlook: Australian housing remains structurally undersupplied with strong population growth, but the residential cycle has cooled through FY26 on cumulative rate rises and tax-policy uncertainty; KPMG forecasts national house prices -1.1% in 2026 before +3.4% in 2027, with units more resilient. Industrial/logistics sentiment remains the strongest A-REIT sub-sector, while office and discretionary retail are more cautious; essentials-based retail continues to perform well.
macro_factors.cyclicality: High for the Development/residential segment (tied to mortgage rates, consumer confidence, land supply); moderate-to-low for the Investment Management segment (contracted rental income with long WALEs, though Workplace is exposed to office-sector oversupply)
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: High - directly affects (1) housing affordability and MPC/LLC settlement volumes and pricing, (2) Stockland's own cost of debt (rising from 5.3% to ~5.9% average in FY27), and (3) capitalisation rates used to value the investment portfolio

recent_developments.event: FY26 full-year results: FFO of $892m (+10.4%), FFO per security 36.9c at top end of guidance (36.0-37.0c); statutory profit $994m (+20.2%); distribution 25.2 cps in line with FY25; gearing 22.7%; DRP suspended for 2H26
FY27 guidance issued: FFO per security of 38.0-39.0 cents, distribution flat at 25.2 cps; growth expected across Group to more than offset a lower FFO contribution from MPC versus the FY26 peak
Formed strategic partnership with Morgan Stanley Real Estate Investing to grow a ~$250m portfolio of convenience retail assets within Stockland communities
Expanded Logistics partnership with M&G Real Estate via transfer of two assets (Coopers Paddock NSW, Willawong Qld) valued at $438m combined

Finalised the Stockland EdgeConneX 50/50 Data Centres partnership; secured ~450MW of power across three sites (MPark NSW, Cherry Lane and Brooklyn Vic) with a further four pipeline sites, three included in the NSW Government's Investment Delivery Authority fast-track approval process

Formed Stockland M&G Land Lease Partnership, seeded with two Victorian communities (Halcyon Jardin, Halcyon Evergreen), ~$200m gross asset value; expanded Invesco land lease partnership; Mercer bought out Mitsubishi Estate Asia's stake in the Stockland Residential Rental Partnership
Board succession: incoming Chairman Robert (Bob) Johnston announced to succeed Tom Pockett, effective from the conclusion of the October 2026 AGMs

3Q26 operational update: FY26 FFO and DPS guidance maintained; MPC net sales +43% and LLC net sales +162% vs pcp; gearing expected to move toward midpoint of 20-30% target; $400m 7.5-year Medium Term Note issued

Federal Budget announced abolition of negative gearing for established dwellings purchased after 12 May 2026 (effective 1 July 2027) and CGT discount reform; new builds remain exempt, a relative positive for Stockland's development pipeline
RBA resumed a monetary tightening cycle, raising mortgage rates and contributing to moderating buyer sentiment noted in Stockland's 2H26 MPC sales commentary

items.notes: Growth across the Group expected to more than offset a lower FFO contribution from the MPC business in FY27 relative to FY26

Alongside growing rental and fee income streams

First financial contribution from the Stockland EdgeConneX partnership expected in FY27; revaluation gains on properties under development to be recognised in FFO from FY27 once monetised via partnering/divestment

guidance.management_commentary: CEO Tarun Gupta and Chairman Tom Pockett noted the FY26 result was at the top end of guidance, driven by a step-change in MPC/LLC settlement volumes and growth in capital partnering fee income, and expressed confidence that growth across Logistics, Retail, Data Centres and Commercial Development will more than offset a lower FY27 MPC contribution. Management explicitly flagged that housing demand has normalised from cyclical highs and that H2 FY26 MPC sales momentum moderated due to cumulative interest rate increases and uncertainty from Federal Budget tax changes, while noting cancellation/default rates remain below long-run averages and incentives remain below long-run levels outside select Victorian projects. All forward guidance is stated subject to no material change in market conditions.

bull_case: FY27 guidance of 38.0-39.0 cps FFO implies continued double-digit-adjacent growth even as the MPC settlement peak normalises, evidencing genuine diversification of earnings drivers (Logistics, LLC, Data Centres, Commercial Development)

Capital-partnering platform (M&G, Invesco, Mercer, Morgan Stanley Real Estate Investing, EdgeConneX) is scaling fee income (+20% in FY26) while reducing Stockland's own capital intensity and improving returns on invested capital
New Data Centres platform (~450MW secured, further pipeline) taps a structurally growing AI/digital infrastructure theme using Stockland's existing land bank at limited incremental capital cost
Strong balance sheet (22.7% gearing, A3 stable rating, $3.2bn liquidity) provides flexibility to acquire land and fund development through a cyclical downturn while peers may be capital constrained

Structural undersupply of Australian housing plus a new-build exemption from the 2027 negative-gearing changes support medium-term demand for Stockland's core masterplanned communities and land lease product
bear_case: Over 60% of FFO is tied to the cyclical residential/land-lease development business; FY26 settlement volumes appear to represent a cyclical peak, and management already guides to lower MPC lot volumes and margin in FY27
Rising interest rates (RBA tightening resumed Feb 2026, cost of debt rising to ~5.9% in FY27) squeeze both buyer affordability for new lots and Stockland's own funding costs simultaneously

Workplace/office portfolio occupancy has fallen materially (91.1% to 86.6%) reflecting structural oversupply, and monetising this exposure via change-of-use conversion carries execution and timing risk

New growth platforms (Data Centres, expanded Commercial Development, additional capital partnerships) are unproven at scale, and their financial contribution depends on continued institutional capital appetite and successful planning/power approvals

Statutory profit is materially inflated by non-cash investment property revaluation gains ($202m in FY26); a housing or capitalisation-rate downturn could reverse these gains and pressure NTA and reported earnings
